newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds end week quietly but in positive mood.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds end week quietly but in positive mood.

text.p: 1130 GMT - Issuance slowed on Friday due to the Independence Day holiday in the U.S.
** Bankers said few firm deals were lined up for next week, but the market's mood was positive.
** Five-year dollar bonds were expected, as well as 10-year mark paper after a successful 3.0 billion mark bond from Italy.
** NTT Corp is due to launch a 10-year Euroyen bond.
The primary market slowed on Friday due to a holiday in the U.S., but ended the week on a positive note.
"The market has ended the week on a firm tone, so we are expecting more activity next week," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said.
"There are few definite deals lined up, though," he said.
Spreads on dollar Eurobonds have remained steady despite a rally in U.S. Treasuries after June payrolls data showed a rise below expectations, dampening prospects of an August interest rate rise.
Bankers said the five-year dollar sector was still attractive to investors.

In marks, there could be more long-dated issuance after Italy's blow-out 3.0 billion mark 10-year bond launched on Thursday, bankers said, although borrowers would not be able to priced the bonds too aggressively.
"There might be more 10-year mark issuance, but Italy was so successful because it was a strategic issue and well-priced," a Frankfurt-based syndicate manager said.
"It might be more difficult for an opportunistic borrower to issue a successful 10-year deal," he said.

NTT Corp is expected to issue a 10-year Euroyen bond, a mandate for which was awarded on Thursday. The deal is expected to be for between 75 and 100 billion yen and could be launched next week via Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley.

NTT had been expected to issue a dollar bond, and some bankers said the choice of yen was surprising because a large proportion of Euroyen is bought by central banks who are not able to buy corporate debt.
